docs.text: Zhu, Weiqiang, and Gregory C. Beroza. "PhaseNet: a deep-neural-network-based seismic arrival-time picking method." Geophysical Journal International 216.1 (2019): 261-273.

docs.title: SurfQuake Plotting and Interactive Commands
docs.text:
SurfQuake includes an interactive plotting tool designed for seismological work. It is much more than a viewer: in the same window you can look at your waveforms, pick phases, mark reference times, select time windows, process the traces, and run analyses (spectra, spectrograms, wavelets, beamforming, particle motion, cross-correlation...) without leaving the plot. Everything you do is stored in the trace headers and can be saved with the processed data.

The same tool also produces publication figures, and it can run without a screen to save the figures of thousands of traces automatically.

This page explains:

  1. How to open the plot and how a session works.
  2. Picking mode: keys and mouse actions on the figure.
  3. Plot types: standard pages, record sections and overlays.
  4. Command prompt: processing and analysis commands typed in the terminal.
  5. Configuration file: every option of the plot.
  6. Saving figures and data.

docs.title: Opening the plot
docs.text:
The plot opens with the processing commands quick, processing and processing_daily when they run in interactive mode (without -a). The plotting options are given with --plot_config:

surfquake make_config -c plotting_config -o ./configs

surfquake quick -w "./data/*" -c ./configs/typical_config.yaml --plot_config ./configs/plotting_config.yaml

The plot is optional for these commands: without --plot_config the default options are used. If you also give an inventory (-i), the array commands (beam, smap) can use the station coordinates.

Fast plotting

For long or numerous traces, -f / --fast draws every trace as a decimated min/max envelope (SAC QDP style). It is much faster, with less detail in the drawn line. With a number, e.g. -f 10, the traces are also decimated before processing, keeping one sample out of 10 (without anti-alias filter: for viewing only, not for analysis).

docs.title: How a session works
docs.text:
A session alternates between two modes:

  • Picking mode (the default): you interact with the figure using the keyboard and the mouse. Picks, references and time windows are set here.
  • Command prompt mode: press v on the figure, and type commands in the terminal (>> prompt). Type p to return to picking mode.
           ┌──────────────── v ────────────────┐
           │                                   ▼
   ┌───────────────┐                  ┌─────────────────┐
   │ Picking mode  │                  │ Command prompt  │
   │ (figure)      │                  │ (terminal, >>)  │
   └───────────────┘                  └─────────────────┘
           ▲                                   │
           └──── p, or after a command that ───┘
                 modifies the traces

When you close the figure window, the terminal asks what to do next:

[Prompt] Finished processing. Type 'c' to continue, 'r' to reprocess this event, or 'e' to exit:
  • c: continue with the next event or time span (processing, processing_daily), or finish (quick).
  • r: reprocess the same data again, re-reading the config file. Useful to try new parameters.
  • e: exit.

docs.title: Picking mode
docs.text: Each subplot shows one trace with its id, and the traces are split into pages of traces_per_fig traces. The keyboard and mouse act on the subplot under the mouse pointer, so place the mouse over a trace before pressing a key.

docs.title: Keys and mouse actions
docs.text:
Key / action What it does n / b Next / previous page. Double left-click Add a pick at that time. The terminal asks for the phase and polarity, e.g. P,U, S,D or just Pg. 1 / 2 / 3 Quick P pick with polarity ? / U (up) / D (down). 4 / 5 / 6 Quick S pick with polarity ? / U / D. e Pick at the mouse position, typing the phase and polarity in the terminal (as the double click). Not available with the Qt5Agg backend. d / Del / Backspace Delete the pick under the cursor. c Clear all picks. w Add a reference time (green dashed line) at the mouse position, on all the traces. p Remove the last reference time (from all the traces). m does the same. u / i Set the start / end of the analysis time window at the mouse position. Right-click drag Select the analysis time window by dragging. v Open the command prompt in the terminal. Esc / Enter Close the current auxiliary figure (spectrum, spectrogram, slowness map...).

The table of shortcuts is printed in the terminal when the figure opens (show_help: true).

docs.title: Picks
docs.text:
Every pick is stored in the header of its trace, in trace.stats.picks, as a dictionary:

{
    "time": 1727123830.321,   # UTC timestamp of the pick
    "phase": "P",             # phase name: P, S, Pg, Sn...
    "amplitude": 3.21e-05,    # amplitude of the trace at the pick time
    "polarity": "U"           # U (up), D (down) or ? (unknown)
}

They are also written, each time you pick, to the file set by pick_output_file (default ./picks.csv). This file is a phase table in the NonLinLoc observation format (station, component, phase, first motion, date and time, amplitude...), which is the input of surfquake locate. A pick file can be loaded back on the plot with auto_load_pick_file: true or with the command load_picks.

See Trace Header for all the header fields and how to use them in Python.

docs.title: Reference times
docs.text: A reference time (w) is a time mark common to all the traces, stored in trace.stats.references as a list of UTC timestamps. Use it to cut all the traces around the same time (cut --reference), or as a time tag for your own scripts.

docs.title: The analysis time window
docs.text: Many commands work on a time window: the spectral analysis (spectrum, spectrogram, cwt, coh), save_tf, beam, smap, pm, wiener and cut without arguments. Set it with u (start) and i (end), or by dragging with the right mouse button. If no window is set, the whole traces are used where possible.

docs.title: Plot types
docs.text:
plot_type Layout Use it for standard One trace per subplot, traces_per_fig subplots per page. Picking, inspection, all the interactive work. record Record section: all the traces in one axis, ordered by epicentral distance (needs event information in the headers, e.g. from surfquake processing -e). Following phases across a network, moveout, EGFs and cross-correlations. overlay All the traces superimposed in one axis. Comparing waveforms: co-located sensors, repeating events, aligned traces.

Change it in the configuration file or from the prompt with plot_type record.

Record section options:

  • record_option: dates (absolute UTC time, with the theoretical arrivals drawn as curves), seconds (seconds from the start of each trace), or egf (lag time, with a red dashed line at t = 0, for empirical Green's functions and cross-correlations).
  • scale_factor: amplitude multiplier of the traces. Increase it to make the traces overlap their neighbours.

docs.title: Command prompt (v key)
docs.text:
Press v on the figure to open the SurfQuake console in the terminal. It lets you process and analyse the displayed traces with short commands, and see the result immediately.

=======================================================
 Command Line Interface Activated
=======================================================
[INFO] Type 'help' to see command line options or 'p' return to picking mode
>>

docs.title: Rules of the prompt
docs.text:
• help lists all the commands; help <command> shows its syntax and examples. Always check help <command>: it is the most up-to-date reference.
  • Trace indices refer to the traces of the current page: 0 is the first subplot, 1 the second... Several traces: a list (0,2) or a range (1-3). all means all the displayed traces.
  • Commands that modify the traces (filter, rmean, taper, normalize, flip, reverse, remove_spikes, wiener, cut, rotate, shift, concat, algebra, xcorr, conv, deconv, runpy, back2future, plot_type) redraw the figure and return to picking mode. Look at the result and press v again to continue.
  • Analysis commands (spectrum, spectrogram, cwt, coh, beam, smap, stack, pm) open an auxiliary figure and do not modify the traces. You stay in the prompt.
  • Close auxiliary figures with Esc or Enter, not with the window's close button: otherwise the prompt may freeze and you cannot return to picking mode.
  • The arrow keys recall previous commands; history lists them.
  • Values with spaces are written in quotes, e.g. cut --start "2024-01-01 12:00:00" --end "2024-01-01 12:01:00".
  • back2future undoes all the processing of the session (it needs back2future: true in the configuration).

docs.title: Navigation and session
docs.text: Command Description n / b Next / previous page. p Return to picking mode. back2future / b2f Restore the traces as they were loaded, undoing all the processing. Needs back2future: true in the configuration. history [N] Show the last N commands (default 10). info Print the headers of the traces (as surfquake info), including picks and event information. exit Close the interactive session.

docs.title: Signal processing
docs.text: Command Syntax Description rmean rmean [--method simple|linear|constant|demean|polynomial|spline] Remove the mean or trend (default simple). taper taper [--type <window>] [--max_percentage <f>] Taper the trace ends (default cosine, 0.05). filter filter <type> <fmin> <fmax> [--corners N] [--zerophase True|False] [--ripple R] [--rp R] [--rs R] Butterworth bandpass, highpass, lowpass, or cheby1, cheby2, elliptic, bessel. For highpass and lowpass give both frequencies; only the relevant one is used. normalize / norm normalize [--mode trace|global] trace: every trace peaks at 1. global: all traces divided by the largest amplitude, keeping relative amplitudes (use it with sharey: true). remove_spikes remove_spikes [--window <s>] [--sigma <f>] Hampel filter: samples further than sigma robust deviations from the moving median are replaced by it (defaults 1 s, 5). wiener wiener [--ncoeff n] [--mu off|on|v] [--epsilon off|on|e] [--update sac|lms] [--start t --end t] Prediction-error (SAC WIENER) filter, designed on the selected time window, which must contain noise only. Whitens the noise and enhances onsets. flip flip [<index>|all] Invert the polarity. reverse reverse [<index>|all] Reverse the traces in time. cut cut cut --phase <name> <before> <after> cut --reference <before> <after> cut --start "<UTC>" --end "<UTC>" Trim the traces to the selected time window, around a pick, around the last reference time, or between two dates (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS). concat concat Merge the segments of the same channel (gaps interpolated). rotate rotate NE->RT rotate NE->RT <baz> rotate ZNE->LQT <baz> [inc] rotate ->ZNE Rotate the components: with the back-azimuth from the headers (great circle), or with a given back-azimuth and inclination. shift shift --phase <name> shift --phase_theo <name> Align the traces on a picked phase, or on a theoretical arrival (needs event information, surfquake processing -e). algebra algebra --expression <formula> New traces from an expression of tr1, tr2..., e.g. algebra --expression sqrt(tr1**2 + tr2**2). See Processing Stream. write write --folder_path <path> [--all] Write the displayed traces (or all with --all) in HDF5, keeping picks, references and event information.

docs.title: Spectral analysis
docs.text:
These commands use the selected time window if there is one. See Time-Frequency Analysis.

Command Syntax Description spectrum / sp spectrum <index>|all [loglog|xlog|ylog|linlin] [--mode m] [--order n] [--nsig n] Amplitude spectrum. Modes: fft (default), multitaper, burg, yule, covar, modcovar, minvar, music, ev. spectrogram / spec spectrogram <index> [<win_s> <overlap_%>] [<clip_dB>] [--method multitaper|fft] [--nw n] [--dates] Spectrogram (default 5 s windows, 50 % overlap, multitaper). cwt cwt <index> <cm|mh|pa> <param> [<fmin> <fmax>] [<clip_dB>] [--dates] Continuous wavelet transform (scalogram). coh / tf coh [--ref i] [--kind both|transfer|coherence] [--method welch|multitaper] [--win s] [--overlap %] [--fmin f] [--fmax f] Coherence and transfer function with respect to a reference trace. save_tf save_tf <spectrum|spectrogram|cwt|coh> <index>|all --folder_path <path> [options] Save the result to disk, to plot it later with surfquake specplot or read it in Python.

docs.title: Array processing and correlation
docs.text: Command Syntax Description beam beam [--fmin f] [--fmax f] [--smax s] [--grid g] [--win s] [--overlap r] FK beamforming in sliding windows over the selected time window: relative power, slowness and back-azimuth. Needs the inventory (-i). In the figure, point at a power peak, press 1–6 to choose the method and e to see its slowness map. See Beamforming. smap smap [--method FK|CAPON|MTP.COHERENCE|MUSIC] [--fmin f] [--fmax f] [--smax s] [--grid g] [--nsignals n] Slowness map of the selected time window. stack stack [<indices>|all] [--method mean|sum|pw:k|root:k] Stack traces (cut to their common window) and show the result: linear mean, sum, phase-weighted (pw:2) or n-th root (root:4). xcorr xcorr [--ref i] [--mode full|same|valid] [--normalize full|naive] [--trim True|False] Cross-correlate the traces with a reference trace. conv conv [--ref i] [--mode full|same|valid] [--trim True|False] Convolve the traces with a reference trace. deconv / deconvolve deconv [--ref i] [--water c] [--gauss a] [--tshift s] [--normalize True|False] [--trim True|False] Water-level deconvolution by a reference trace (e.g. receiver functions).

docs.title: Polarization, picks and display
docs.text: Command Syntax Description pm pm Particle motion of every complete three-component station (ZNE, Z12, ZYX) in the selected time window. See Particle Motion. load_picks load_picks --file <path> Load picks from a phase file (NonLinLoc format) and draw them. plot_type plot_type standard|record|overlay Change the layout.

docs.title: Your own scripts
docs.text: Command Syntax Description runpy runpy <script.py> Run your own Python function process(stream) on the loaded traces; what it returns replaces them. See Scripts.

docs.title: Example session
docs.text:
>> filter bandpass 1.0 10.0 --corners 4 --zerophase True
   (the figure is redrawn: look at it, set a window with 'u' and 'i', then press 'v')
>> spectrum all loglog --mode multitaper
   (close the spectrum with Esc)
>> spectrogram 0 3.0 75 --dates
>> save_tf spectrogram 0 --win 3.0 --overlap 75 --folder_path ./time_freq
>> cut --reference 10 60
   (back in picking mode: pick the P and S waves with the keys 1-6, then press 'v')
>> write --folder_path ./processed_h5
>> p

docs.title: Configuration file
docs.text:
Create a fully commented configuration file with:

surfquake make_config -c plotting_config -o ./configs

Every key is optional: a key you remove takes its default value. All keys go under the plotting: section.

plotting:
  plot_type: standard
  traces_per_fig: 6
  sort_by: false
  sharey: false
  show_legend: true
  record_option: dates
  scale_factor: 1
  show_arrivals: false
  pick_output_file: ./picks.csv
  auto_load_pick_file: false
  show_info_picks: false
  show_crosshair: false
  plot_output_path: null
  format_save: png
  show_plot: true
  show_help: true
  fast: false
  fast_points: 1000
  back2future: false
  backend: TkAgg
  rcparams:
    lines.linewidth: 0.5

YAML reminders

Booleans are true / false, and "nothing" is null. Do not end a line with a comma: fast: false, is read as the text "false,", which counts as true.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text: Key Default Description plot_type standard standard, record or overlay (see Plot types). traces_per_fig 6 Traces (subplots) per page, standard only. sort_by false Order of the traces: distance, backazimuth (both need event information in the headers) or false (input order). sharey false true: the same amplitude scale in all the subplots, to compare amplitudes between traces. false: each trace is scaled independently. show_legend true Show the trace id in each subplot.

docs.title: Record section
docs.text: Key Default Description record_option dates X axis: dates (UTC), seconds (from the start of each trace) or egf (lag time with a line at t = 0). scale_factor 1 Amplitude multiplier of the traces.

docs.title: Arrivals and picks
docs.text: Key Default Description show_arrivals false Draw the origin time (blue) and the theoretical arrivals (green, dashed, labelled) stored in the headers. pick_output_file ./picks.csv File where the picks are written (NonLinLoc phase format). auto_load_pick_file false Load the picks of pick_output_file when the figure opens. show_info_picks false Show a box with the information of the current pick. show_crosshair false Dashed lines following the mouse. single: vertical line in all subplots and horizontal line in the one under the mouse (recommended; true means this). vertical, horizontal (useful with sharey: true), all, or false.

docs.title: Saving figures
docs.text: Key Default Description plot_output_path null Folder where the figures are saved. null: not saved. If the folder does not exist, you are offered to create it. format_save png Image format: png, pdf, svg, jpg... show_plot true true: interactive window. false: headless (batch) mode: nothing is displayed, all the pages are written to plot_output_path, and no question is asked.

docs.title: Performance and interaction
docs.text: Key Default Description show_help true Print the table of shortcuts when the figure opens. fast false Quick-and-dirty plotting: min/max decimated lines, much faster for long traces. The option -f of quick activates it too. fast_points 1000 Points (min/max pairs) per trace in fast mode. back2future false Keep a copy of the loaded traces so back2future can undo all the processing. It doubles the memory used by the traces.

docs.title: Backend
docs.text: Key Default Description backend TkAgg Graphical engine: TkAgg (most robust, recommended), MacOSX (macOS only, recommended there), Qt5Agg (fast, but picking and interactive commands may fail; the e key is disabled). Ignored in headless mode, which uses Agg.

docs.title: Style (Matplotlib rcParams)
docs.text:
Any Matplotlib rcParam can be set under rcparams to adapt the figures to your publication style. They apply to the standard, overlay and record plots; unknown keys are ignored with a warning. The time axis format, the scientific notation of the Y axis and the figure size are fixed by SurfQuake.

plotting:
  rcparams:
    xtick.labelsize: 7
    ytick.labelsize: 7
    xtick.direction: in
    xtick.minor.visible: true
    lines.linewidth: 0.5
    legend.fontsize: 8
    font.family: serif
    savefig.dpi: 300

docs.title: Figures
docs.text:
show_plot plot_output_path Result true null Displayed, not saved. true ./figures Displayed and saved. false ./figures Not displayed, all pages saved (batch mode, for scripts and servers). false null Nothing is shown or saved.

In automatic mode (-a), the figures are only produced in batch mode (show_plot: false with a plot_output_path). The figures are named after the plot type, the page and the start time of the plotted data: sqProject_page<NNN>_<YYYYmmdd-HHMMSS>.<format> for standard pages, sqProject_record_page... and sqProject_overlay_page... for the other types (e.g. sqProject_record_page000_20220201-020256.png). Each event or time span gets its own figures, and if a file already exists _1, _2... is added, so figures are never overwritten.

docs.title: Picks, references and processed traces
docs.text:
• Picks are written to pick_output_file each time you pick, and stored in the trace headers.
  • Picks, references and event information travel with the traces in their headers. To keep them, write the traces in HDF5: from the prompt with write --folder_path <path>, or automatically with -o <folder> and -a. See Trace Header.
  • Analysis results (spectra, spectrograms, scalograms, coherence) are saved with save_tf, and beamforming and particle motion results with their config steps.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Problem Solution A key does nothing Place the mouse over a trace (inside a subplot) before pressing it, and make sure the figure window has the focus. The prompt is frozen after closing a spectrum or other figure Close auxiliary figures with Esc / Enter, not with the window button. After a command, the prompt disappeared Commands that modify the traces redraw the figure and return to picking mode. Press v again. back2future does not work Set back2future: true in the configuration file. sort_by: distance or record does nothing The traces need event information in their headers: use surfquake processing with an event file and an inventory. Picking or the prompt fail with Qt5Agg Use backend: TkAgg (or MacOSX on macOS). Slow plots Use fast: true (or -f), fewer traces_per_fig, or cut the traces first.

docs.title: Probability Power Spectral Density Functions (PPSD)
docs.text: The Probability Power Spectral Density Functions (Peterson, 1993; McNamara & Buland, 2004) are used to characterize the background seismic noise.

docs.title: PPSD DB CLI
docs.text:
This command creates a file-based database that stores Probability Power Spectral Density Functions (PPSD) in a pickle file. The file is basically a dictionary with keys net, station channel and the ObsPy object with the PPSD.

        Key Arguments:
            -p,  --project_file        [REQUIRED] Path to project file (previously generated using surfquake project)
            -i,  --inventory_file      [REQUIRED] Path to stations metadata (XML or RESP)
            -s,  --save_file           [REQUIRED] Path to save the data base
            -le, --length              [OPTIONAL] Length of data segments passed to psd in seconds (default 3600)
            -ov, --overlap             [OPTIONAL] Overlap in percentage of segments passed to psd (default 50)
            -sm, --smoothing           [OPTIONAL] PSDs are averaged over a octave at each central freq (default 1)
            -n,  --net                 [OPTIONAL] project net filter (Default: *, Example WM)
            -s,  --station             [OPTIONAL] project station filter (Default: *, Example ARNO)
            -ch, --channel             [OPTIONAL] project channel filter (Default: *, Example BH?)

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: >> surfquake ppsdDB -p [project_file] -i [inventory_file] -s [save_file] -le [Time window length] -sm [Smoothing] -ov [Overlap] -pr [Period] -nt [Net Selection]  -st [Station Selection] -ch [Channel Selection]

docs.text: >> surfquake ppsdDB -h

docs.text: >> surfquake ppsdDB -p "./ppsd_test" -i "./meta/metadata.xml" -s "./output/test.pkl"

    ----------

docs.title: Plotting & Statistics
docs.text: Reads a PPSD pickle database produced by ppsdDB and generates publication-quality figures.

docs.title: PPSD Plot CLI
docs.text:
Three plot modes are available:

    heatmap    Probability density colormaps (classic PPSD view).
               One figure per group of --spp stations.  Use --all to
               iterate automatically over every station group.

    variation  Diurnal or seasonal noise variation shown as a contour
               plot (mode amplitude vs hour-of-day or month).

    comparison Overlay mean / median / mode curves for a wildcard
               selection of stations and channels on shared axes.
               One panel per component (Z, N, E …) or a single panel.

    Key Arguments:
        -d,  --db_file         [REQUIRED] Path to the PPSD pickle database
        -m,  --mode            [REQUIRED] Plot mode: heatmap | variation | comparison
        -sd, --save_dir        [OPTIONAL] Directory to save figures (one per page)
        -sp, --save_path       [OPTIONAL] Single output file path (heatmap p.0 or comparison)
        -sf, --save_format     [OPTIONAL] Figure format: png | pdf | svg          (png)
        -nt, --net             [OPTIONAL] Network wildcard filter                  (*)
        -st, --station         [OPTIONAL] Station wildcard filter                  (*)
        -ch, --channel         [OPTIONAL] Channel wildcard filter, e.g. BH?        (*)
        -t0, --starttime       [OPTIONAL] Start of time window, ISO format
        -t1, --endtime         [OPTIONAL] End of time window, ISO format

      heatmap / variation only:
        --spp                  [OPTIONAL] Stations per page                          (3)
        --page                 [OPTIONAL] Page index (0-based); ignored with --all   (0)
        --all                  [OPTIONAL] Iterate over all station groups
        --variation            [OPTIONAL] Variation type: Diurnal | Seasonal  (Diurnal)
        --mean                 [OPTIONAL] Overlay mean curve
        --mode                 [OPTIONAL] Overlay mode curve
        --nhnm                 [OPTIONAL] Overlay NHNM reference
        --nlnm                 [OPTIONAL] Overlay NLNM reference
        --earthquakes          [OPTIONAL] Overlay earthquake model lines
        --min_mag              [OPTIONAL] Minimum magnitude for eq. models          (0.0)
        --max_mag              [OPTIONAL] Maximum magnitude for eq. models         (10.0)
        --min_dist             [OPTIONAL] Minimum distance for eq. models (km)      (0.0)
        --max_dist             [OPTIONAL] Maximum distance for eq. models (km)   (10000)

      comparison only:
        --stats                [OPTIONAL] Comma-separated list: mean,median,mode   (mean)
        --layout               [OPTIONAL] by_component | single          (by_component)

>> surfquake ppsdPlot -d "./output/test.pkl" --all -m heatmap --mean --nhnm --nlnm --earthquakes --min_mag 1.0 --max_mag 3.0
